dialect.detail: IBM mainframe-style batch COBOL, likely compiled on a mainframe or compatible environment. Uses RETURN-CODE special register, FILE STATUS codes, and ASSIGN TO SYS00n-style DDnames typical of IBM JCL/mainframe conventions. Spanish-language comments and identifiers suggest Latin American mainframe shop (possibly Colombian banking).

purpose.domain_detail: ETL/EGL transformation program merging two input files (CN255SE - transaction notifications, CN285SE - device/network data) to produce an output file (RD457SS) with enriched transaction records. Context suggests Colombian or Latin American banking.
purpose.summary: This batch program performs a merge-join (ETL) between two sequential input files keyed on account number. It reads CN255SE (transaction notifications) and CN285SE (device/network data), matches records by account number key, and writes merged records to output file RD457SS. It tracks read and write counts and displays summary statistics on completion.

notable_features: Merge/join logic on two sequential files by key comparison (WK-LLAVE1 vs WK-LLAVE2)
FILE STATUS error handling with '97' (IBM file-not-found open status)
RETURN-CODE special register for job step return code
CALL to external utility 'GEC002' for date retrieval
ACCEPT ... FROM TIME for system time
PERFORM THRU paragraph exit pattern throughout
verdict.notes: Source uses tab characters for indentation in some DATA DIVISION entries (mixed tabs/spaces), though the overall format is fixed-column. The program appears to be a student or training exercise ('Grupo 5 COBIW', 'COBIW' likely a COBOL course) but is written in production style with proper error handling, file status checks, and structured logic. Domain is clearly banking/finance based on field names (NUM-CTA=account number, NUM-TRANSAC=transaction number).
